text:
The design misses only bandwidth: 40 MHz simulated against the 48 MHz target. It has headroom on gain (1.1 dB), noise (212 vs 270 fA/√Hz) and power (40.6 vs 54 µW). The model printed no predictions, so the bandwidth gains below are first-order estimates.

- **Current up:** raising the front CS current Ics from 12 to about 14 µA raises gm1 and the loop gain. Bandwidth scales roughly with √gm1, so expect about +8%.
- **Rf down:** lowering Rf from 460 kΩ to about 420 kΩ costs about 0.8 dB of transimpedance (113.1 → about 112.3 dB, limit 112) and buys roughly +5% bandwidth.
- **Power budget:** the 54 µW limit allows 30 µA at 1.8 V. The reference takes 10 µA, which leaves 20 µA for Ics + Isf + Ip. The starting point uses 14 + 4.5 + 1.0 = 19.5 µA, about 53 µW. I narrowed the Ics bound to 15 µA so the search stays near that limit.

These two moves together give roughly +13%, short of the +19% needed. I'm relying on the refiner's other knobs to close the rest, which is why I chose refine rather than edit.

```json
{"action": "refine",
 "reason": "Only BW misses (~16%). Margins exist in gain, noise and power. Raise Ics (more gm1/loop gain), trim Rf toward 112 dB limit, cut Ip, lower Cf. Keep Ics+Isf+Ip <= 20 uA for power.",
 "params": {"Ics": 14e-6, "Ip": 1.0e-6, "Rf": 4.2e5, "Cf": 0.3e-15, "Isf": 4.5e-6},
 "bounds": {"Ics": [11e-6, 15e-6], "Ip": [0.7e-6, 2e-6], "Rf": [4.05e5, 4.8e5], "Cf": [0.05e-15, 5e-15], "Isf": [3e-6, 6e-6]}}
```
